reason: Both satisfy the hard requirements, but Response B is more rigorous about backup timing: it takes a full backup before the rehearsal (step 4) and a second, freshly-consistent backup at the write-freeze point (step 8) immediately before cutover, so rollback (step 11) restores from a backup taken at the actual cutoff rather than one taken before the bulk load began as in Response A, which could be stale by the time of cutover. B also explicitly calls for rehearsing the rollback procedure itself and adds a schema-freeze/go-no-go gate, making its runbook slightly more production-ready.
